html:
SMTO-FIL-0005 — The file operation was stopped before it finished

GUID: 615e5781-70c8-49f5-a995-456288774415
Slug: file-cancelled
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The copy, save or transfer stopped because its Task or Activity was stopped. Some files may already have been copied or changed before it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether you or someone else selected Stop on this Task or Activity, and wait until it shows as stopped. The file work ends when its Task stops, and it must be fully stopped before you check the results.
  2. Ask SMTO to list the destination folder, and for a move the original folder too, to see what was already done. Files finished before the stop stay in place and aren't undone.
  3. Ask SMTO to redo only the files that are missing or incomplete. Repeating the whole operation could create duplicates or overwrite files that already finished.

What success looks like

  • The destination holds exactly the files you expect, with none missing or doubled.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't restart the whole operation until you've checked what was already done.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A cooperative cancellation check found the run or Activity cancellation event set during a file or transfer operation, so it stopped; effects completed before the stop remain.

What this means

  • The owned cancellation event was set when a file/transfer cancellation checkpoint ran. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The owned cancellation event was set when a file/transfer cancellation checkpoint ran.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect executed, changed, partial and cleanup facts from the original operation; cancellation does not roll back all earlier work.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the cancellation source (run or Activity stop) and that the original operation has ended. Inspect changed_paths, residual_paths and any transfer results for partial effects, and reconcile the destination before issuing any new change.
  • Inspect the cancellation source and any partial destination before starting new work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original owner has stopped and any partial or completed destination state is accounted for.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
